prompt: Implement the Decorator pattern: complete the nested Upper and Exclaim classes in TextDecorators, each wrapping another Text and transforming its render() result so decorators can be stacked in any order.
explanation: A decorator implements the same interface as the object it wraps and holds a reference to it, so from the outside a decorated Text is indistinguishable from a plain one. Each render() call delegates inward first (inner.render()) and then applies its own twist on the way back out, which is why decorators compose to any depth. The order of wrapping matters only when the transformations interact -- Upper over Exclaim still yields "OK!" because "!" has no upper-case form.
hints: Each decorator needs a private final Text field assigned from the constructor parameter.
In render(), call inner.render() first, then transform that result (toUpperCase() or + "!").
Do not touch PlainText -- stacking works because a decorator's constructor accepts ANY Text, including another decorator.
